s01.visual: Paper card: “TRY THIS.” slams in word by word, orange underline draws on, pointing finger wiggles in. Slow push-in.
Close-up: your finger (yellow sleeve) whips in and tickles a giant cartoon foot; tickle marks pop; label “YOUR FINGER”.
Rando stands bored (half-lidded), “…” bubble, “*itch*” scratch, then a tumbleweed rolls through the room.
Whip-pan to the same foot on teal — now it's your FRIEND's finger; foot starts squirming.
Pattern interrupt: Rando in full meltdown — flailing limbs, burst background, bouncing “HA! HAHA” letters, screen shake.
Split screen YOU vs YOUR FRIEND; checklist pops “SAME SKIN ✓ · SAME TOUCH ✓ · DIFFERENT REACTION”.
Two fingers on paper, magnifying glass sweeps across, big red “?” floats — the open loop.

s02.visual: Navy glitch card “A glitch in the human body”: Rando with RGB-split jitter and scanline bars.
Crowd of 7 diverse randos under falling feathers all burst out laughing — then all try tickling themselves, flat faces. “CAN TICKLE THEMSELVES ✗”.
Skin / foot / fingers icons pop in and get crossed out one by one on each word.
Huge Rando head; X-ray circle reveals the brain inside, sparkles, title “It’s in your brain”.
Brain at a desk with a red pen striking lines out of a document titled REALITY; wall clock ticks.
TITLE CARD: “Why can’t you / tickle yourself?” kinetic type, feather swoops in and tickles the title.

s03.visual: REWIND: calendar flips 2026 → 1971, clock spins backwards, stamp lands.
1971 retro lab: Lawrence Weiskrantz tickles a bare foot poking out of a curtain with a feather; name tag; “HAHA!” from behind.
Hand-drawn bar chart: TICKLINESS — someone else (tall) vs yourself (short).
KNISMESIS: feather glides along a forearm, goosebumps, itchy squiggles.
GARGALESIS: friend pokes Rando's ribs; full laugh, HA letters, shake.
Rando pokes his own ribs, deadpan; “…nope.” bubble; “SELF-GARGALESIS ✗”.
Three puzzled scientists shrug as question marks pop.
Sarah-Jayne Blakemore presents the MRI brain scanner sliding in.
Close-up of a palm while a foam-tipped stick brushes back and forth.
Two panels — EXPERIMENTER MOVES IT / VOLUNTEER MOVES IT — orange highlight slides between them.
Scanner monitor: the brain's touch strip glows orange (someone else) … then fades grey (yourself).
Brain drops on earmuffs and ignores a waving hand saying “hellooo?”.
Side-view brain; the cerebellum pulses orange, circled and labelled (“latin for ‘little brain’”); camera dives in.
Quick-fire vignettes: WALK (walk cycle), TYPE (laptop), CATCH (ball arc into hand).
Spotlight noir: the cerebellum in a detective hat tiptoes across, shifty eyes.
Crystal ball with the cerebellum inside, glowing; “predicting the future”.

s04.visual: Brain fires an envelope down a dotted nerve to Rando; LIFT / MOVE LEFT / PRESS DOWN commands pop as his arm obeys.
Email window To: MUSCLES, CC: BRAIN (ME); the envelope splits in two; red stamp “EFFERENCE COPY”.
Brain's thought bubble shows the predicted feeling with a “simulating…” progress bar.
PREDICTION vs REALITY cards slide in, VS badge, then they slide together and overlap.
Match: green check, “that was just me”, volume knob turns down, speaker waves vanish.
Mismatch: red siren flashes, brain gasps, knob cranks up, waves return, shake.
Friend's hand follows a chaotic dotted path; Rando's eyes chase it; WHERE? HOW HARD? HOW FAST? → laughter.
Rando's thought bubble holds THE PLAN; his own hand traces the exact dotted path. “NO SURPRISE”.
“robots!” — two cute robots bounce in waving, stars burst.
Two-robot setup: left hand drives robot A, signal pulse travels the cable to robot B whose foam tip brushes the right palm. Stopwatch adds +0.1 s, +0.2 s and the pulse visibly lags.
TICKLY-O-METER shoots up; Rando goes from deadpan to giggling.
Direction mismatch: robot arrow rotates away from the hand's arrow; graph draws MISMATCH → TICKLE curve.
Kinetic type: “it’s not about who” (who struck out) → “it’s whether your brain saw it coming”; a big eye glances left-right.

s05.visual: Purple spinning spiral, “it gets weird”, Rando's head wobbles.
Brain at the centre of orbiting senses (eye, speaker, hand, speech): “ALWAYS ON”.
Giant eye makes saccades; a little world panel lurches with every jump (WITHOUT PREDICTION) then stays rock-steady (WHAT YOU SEE).
Equation: EYE MOVES + BRAIN CANCELS IT = STEADY WORLD ✓ (each term pops in).
Night meadow: a cricket chirps huge sound waves, “CHIRP!”, fun fact arrow: “its ears are on its legs!”.
One nerve cell fires; a playhead sweeps a timeline showing hearing dipping exactly on every chirp.
Rando talks (lip flaps + voice waves); thought bubble: brain turning a knob — “YOUR VOICE: TURNED DOWN”.
“why are we ticklish?” — Rando shrugs among question marks; “nobody knows for sure”.
Body map: neck, ribs, feet glow red; a spider drops in and creeps closer; alarm siren; Rando sweats.
Parent tickles a giggling baby; hearts float up.
Rat gets tickled, ultrasonic chirp squiggles (TOO HIGH-PITCHED FOR HUMANS), then chases the hand: “more!”.
Circle of YOU: red arrows from the outside punch in (OUTSIDE = LOUD); an inside arrow gets muted (INSIDE = QUIET).
Swinging “HIDDEN COST” price tag, calendar stamps 2003.
Two volunteers at a table take turns pressing; a balance scale tips each turn; “FAIR?”.
Escalation bar chart grows turn by turn; “≈ +38% EVERY TURN”.
Arrow diagram: WHAT YOU PUSH (big) → WHAT YOU FEEL (small, muted brain) → WHAT THEY FEEL (big).
Back seat of a car: “YOU HIT ME HARDER!”; the sibling gets a halo — “…they might be right”.

s06.visual: Dark room: a neon “THAT WAS ME” sign flickers above a worried brain.
Gentle, respectful illustration (2000): faint wordless voice bubbles drift; puppet strings lower — HEARING VOICES / FEELING CONTROLLED.
Grouped bars: MOST PEOPLE (self much lower) vs THESE PATIENTS (self ≈ someone else).
The “ME” tag on his hand fades and droops; his inner-voice bubble drifts outside his head; “?”.
Two bins: THINGS I DID / THINGS THAT HAPPENED TO ME; objects drop in. Then I DID gets a mute icon and greys out, HAPPENED gets a flag and a spotlight.
Rando in a warm glow: A BODY ✓ · ACTIONS ✓ · A VOICE ✓ — “…that’s yours”.
A feather tickles a theatre curtain open, revealing the brain's hidden gears turning.
Rando jumps out of a box yelling “BOO!” at his mirror reflection, which replies “meh.”

s07.visual: Friend tickles Rando in the sunshine; thought bubble: brain thumbs-up “JUST DOING MY JOB”.
End card: “Randos in 60s” logo writes in, Rando waves, cursor clicks SUBSCRIBE → SUBSCRIBED, bell rings, “see you in the next one”.
